```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Berton_2024_pregnancy_physiology"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/ofid/ofae585>\n")
cat("* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11495486/>\n")
```

Berton 2024 asks when, after delivery, a pharmacokinetic study should be run
so that the postpartum reference fully captures the effect of pregnancy on drug
exposure. To answer it, the authors extended the Basel in-house Matlab
whole-body PBPK framework (Stader 2019) with a pregnant and postpartum virtual
population. They pooled 224 articles, normalised every anatomical,
physiological and enzyme-abundance measurement to its non-pregnant value, and
regressed the fold change on gestational age (Supplementary Table 2). The
population was then verified with seven antiretrovirals and used to show that
drug exposure is mostly back to its pre-pregnancy level 4 to 5 weeks after
delivery.

The packaged model is that **system layer**: the virtual pregnant / postpartum
woman. It has no drug, no dose, no compartments and no ODEs. Every output is an
algebraic function of the `rxode2` time variable, which the model interprets as
**gestational age in weeks**. Delivery is at 40 weeks for every woman, so
`time > 40` is postpartum and `time - 40` is the week after delivery; the
equations were fitted and the population generated over 0 to 66 weeks.

```{r description, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("> ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

## Why the drug layer is not included

The seven drug PBPK models the paper verifies against this population
(ritonavir, efavirenz, rilpivirine, doravirine, dolutegravir, bictegravir and
raltegravir) "were developed previously" in the authors' obese and ageing
papers (Berton 2024 Clin Infect Dis; Stader 2021 Br J Clin Pharmacol) and "were
used without changing any drug parameters". None of their drug parameters is
printed in Berton 2024, and the paper does not describe how the fetoplacental
unit is connected to the PBPK ODEs (its partition coefficient, whether it is a
perfusion-limited organ, how it is fed from the uterine flow). The drug layer
can be added once those inputs are available. A bictegravir PBPK on the 2017
version of the same framework is already in the library
(`Stader_2021_bictegravir_pbpk`); its organ-weight and flow regressions are an
earlier version of the non-pregnant equations used here, so the two models
cannot be chained without re-deriving that PBPK on this population.

# Population

The development and verification data come from 224 published studies of
pregnant and postpartum women (Supplementary Table 1). The authors generated
1000 virtual women across 0 to 66 weeks of gestational age to compare against
the verification data set (Figure 1; Supplementary Figures 1 and 2). The
verification trials (Supplementary Table 3) enrolled pregnant women living with
HIV aged 18 to 44 years, sampled at gestational ages of 13 to 40 weeks and 41
to 80 weeks (postpartum).

The non-pregnant baseline of every woman comes from the framework's age-,
height- and sex-dependent regressions (Supplementary Table 2, citing the Stader
2019 ageing repository of White adults), each with a population CV. Age is the
only covariate; sex is fixed to female.

# Source trace

Every gestational-age coefficient is a point estimate of a regression the
authors fitted in Matlab 2020a; **no standard error or confidence interval is
reported**, so every `ini()` entry is `fixed()`. Equations inherited from other
sources (non-pregnant regressions from Stader 2019; uterus, mammary gland,
fetus, placenta and amniotic fluid from Abduljalil 2012; fetoplacental flow in
the Gaohua 2012 form) are written as constants in `model()`, each with its
Supplementary Table 2 row cited in an in-file comment.

| Output (units) | Supplementary Table 2 rows | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `ht` (cm), `wt_np` (kg) | Body height; Body weight, Non pregnant | age (and height) regressions, CV 3.8% / 15.2% |
| `wt` (kg), `bmi`, `bsa` | Body weight FC; BMI; BSA | quadratic FC in pregnancy and postpartum; DuBois BSA |
| `w_adipose`, `w_brain`, `w_heart`, `w_kidney` (kg) | organ weight + organ weight FC | linear FC, own postpartum line, capped at 1 where printed |
| `w_lung`, `w_bone`, `w_gonads`, `w_skin`, `w_thymus`, `w_gut`, `w_spleen`, `w_pancreas`, `w_liver` (kg) | organ weight; FC = 1 | non-pregnant regression only |
| `w_uterus`, `w_mammary`, `w_muscle` (kg) | Uterus / Mammary gland (FC); Total muscle weight | Abduljalil 2012; both inside muscle |
| `w_plasma`, `w_rbc`, `w_blood` (kg) | Plasma / Red blood cells weight (FC); Blood weight | see Assumptions for the blood-weight row |
| `w_fetus`, `w_placenta`, `w_amniotic`, `w_fetoplacental` (kg) | Foetal / Placental / Amniotic fluid weight | Gompertz, cubic, quintic in GA; 0 after delivery |
| `co` (L/h) | Cardiac output; Cardiac output FC | quadratic FC to 50.9 weeks |
| `fq_*` (% of CO), `q_*` (L/h) | regional flows; Blood flows FC; Brain / Kidney / Uterus blood flow FC; Muscle blood flow; Foetal-placental blood flow | see the flow-budget check below |
| `gfr` (mL/min) | GFR; GFR FC | quadratic FC to 67.5 weeks |
| `hct` (fraction) | HCT; HCT FC | quadratic FC to 65 weeks |
| `hsa`, `agp` (g/L) | Albumin (FC); AAG (FC) | quadratic FC; albumin has its own postpartum line |
| `fc_cyp1a2` ... `fc_ugt1a4` | CYP / UGT FC rows | quadratic FC, 1 after the printed knot; CYP3A5 = CYP3A4 |

```{r ini-table, echo = FALSE}
ui$iniDf |>
  dplyr::filter(is.na(neta1)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Parameter = name,
    Value = signif(est, 6),
    Fixed = ifelse(fix, "yes", "no"),
    Label = label
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gestational-age fold-change coefficients as packaged (all fixed; Berton 2024 Supplementary Table 2).")
```

```{r eta-table, echo = FALSE}
ui$iniDf |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(neta1), neta1 == neta2) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Draw = name,
    Variance = signif(est, 6),
    `CV (%)` = signif(100 * sqrt(est), 4)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual-population draws: Mean x (1 + eta), eta ~ N(0, (CV/100)^2), CVs from Supplementary Table 2.")
```

# Simulation

There is nothing to dose: a solve needs only an observation grid and each
woman's age.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Berton_2024_pregnancy_physiology")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ga_grid <- seq(0, 66, by = 0.5)

# Typical 30-year-old woman (all etas zero).
d_typ <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = ga_grid, evid = 0L, AGE = 30)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, d_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(nrow(sim_typ) == length(ga_grid))

# Typical value at given gestational ages, matched by value rather than by row
# position.
typical_at <- function(ga) {
  idx <- match(ga, sim_typ$time)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(idx))
  sim_typ[idx, , drop = FALSE]
}

# Virtual cohort of 200 women (the per-arm cap for these vignettes), ages drawn
# uniformly over the 18 to 44 years of the verification trials, each followed
# from conception to 26 weeks after delivery.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241018)
set.seed(20241018)
n_women <- 200L
ages <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_women), AGE = runif(n_women, 18, 44))
d_pop <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_women), time = seq(0, 66, by = 1)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(ages, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L)
sim_pop <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, d_pop, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(sim_pop$id) == n_women)
```

# Validation 1: changes at the third trimester

The Results report the third-trimester change relative to non-pregnant women
for several organ weights, cardiac output and the plasma proteins. The typical
woman reproduces them.

```{r val-third-trimester}
base <- typical_at(0)
term <- typical_at(40)
pct <- function(x) round(100 * (term[[x]] / base[[x]] - 1), 1)

tab_t3 <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Adipose weight", "Heart weight", "Kidney weight", "Blood weight",
               "Brain weight", "Cardiac output", "Albumin", "Alpha-1-acid glycoprotein"),
  Output = c("w_adipose", "w_heart", "w_kidney", "w_blood", "w_brain", "co", "hsa", "agp"),
  Published = c(25, 30, 30, 47, -7, 20, -25, -20)
)
tab_t3$Model <- vapply(tab_t3$Output, pct, numeric(1))
tab_t3 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `Published change, % (Results)` = Published,
    `Model at 40 weeks, %` = Model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical 30-year-old woman at 40 weeks vs non-pregnant; published values from the Results text.")

# The published values are rounded figures from the text; every modelled change
# must be within 5 percentage points of them and in the same direction.
stopifnot(
  all(sign(tab_t3$Model) == sign(tab_t3$Published)),
  all(abs(tab_t3$Model - tab_t3$Published) <= 5)
)
```

Cardiac output "returned to baseline 10 weeks after delivery" (Results):

```{r val-co-return}
co_fc <- sim_typ$co / base$co
first_baseline <- min(sim_typ$time[sim_typ$time > 40 & abs(co_fc - 1) < 1e-8])
first_baseline - 40
stopifnot(abs((first_baseline - 40) - 10) <= 1)
```

# Validation 2: Table 1, enzyme abundance and albumin

Table 1 gives, for each enzyme and for albumin, the change at 37 to 40 weeks and
the postpartum week by which it is back to baseline.

```{r val-table1}
fc_cols <- c(CYP1A2 = "fc_cyp1a2", CYP2B6 = "fc_cyp2b6", CYP2C9 = "fc_cyp2c9",
             CYP2C19 = "fc_cyp2c19", CYP2D6 = "fc_cyp2d6", CYP3A4 = "fc_cyp3a4",
             UGT1A1 = "fc_ugt1a1", UGT1A4 = "fc_ugt1a4")
sim_typ$fc_hsa_out <- sim_typ$hsa / base$hsa
fc_cols <- c(fc_cols, Albumin = "fc_hsa_out")

t1_change <- c(CYP1A2 = -44, CYP2B6 = 30, CYP2C9 = 56, CYP2C19 = 24, CYP2D6 = 44,
               CYP3A4 = 69, UGT1A1 = 23, UGT1A4 = 116, Albumin = -25)
t1_weeks <- c(CYP1A2 = 12, CYP2B6 = 11, CYP2C9 = 2, CYP2C19 = 4, CYP2D6 = 11,
              CYP3A4 = 5, UGT1A1 = 6, UGT1A4 = 12, Albumin = 5)

w3740 <- sim_typ$time >= 37 & sim_typ$time <= 40
tab_t1 <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(fc_cols),
  pub_change = t1_change[names(fc_cols)],
  mod_mean = vapply(fc_cols, function(x) 100 * (mean(sim_typ[[x]][w3740]) - 1), numeric(1)),
  mod_40 = vapply(fc_cols, function(x) 100 * (sim_typ[[x]][sim_typ$time == 40] - 1), numeric(1)),
  pub_weeks = t1_weeks[names(fc_cols)],
  mod_weeks = vapply(fc_cols, function(x) {
    post <- sim_typ$time > 40
    # First postpartum time from which the fold change stays at 1.
    off <- sim_typ$time[post][abs(sim_typ[[x]][post] - 1) > 1e-8]
    (if (length(off)) max(off) + 0.5 else 40.5) - 40
  }, numeric(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
tab_t1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(mod_mean, mod_40), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `Table 1 change, %` = pub_change,
    `Model mean 37-40 wk, %` = mod_mean,
    `Model at 40 wk, %` = mod_40,
    `Table 1 back to baseline, pp wk` = pub_weeks,
    `Model back to baseline, pp wk` = mod_weeks
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 1 of Berton 2024 against the typical woman.")

stopifnot(
  # Direction of every change matches Table 1.
  all(sign(tab_t1$mod_mean) == sign(tab_t1$pub_change)),
  # The return-to-baseline week follows from the printed knots and agrees with
  # Table 1 to within one week for all nine variables.
  all(abs(tab_t1$mod_weeks - tab_t1$pub_weeks) <= 1)
)
```

The return-to-baseline weeks agree for all nine variables. The size of the
change is less consistent, and Table 1 does not use one rule for it: the
albumin, CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 entries match the equations at 40
weeks to within 3 percentage points, while the CYP2C9 entry (+56%) matches the
37 to 40 week mean (+59%) and is twice the 40-week value. The CYP2D6 (+44%)
and UGT1A1 (+23%) entries match neither; UGT1A1's +23% is the equation's peak
at about 23 weeks, and UGT1A4's +116% is its value at 37 weeks. Table 1 is
most likely summarised from the observed clinical data or the simulated
population rather than read off the fitted curves; the packaged model follows
the Supplementary Table 2 equations.

# Validation 3: the regional blood-flow budget

Supplementary Table 2 gives regional flows as percent of cardiac output. Most
organs are assumed to keep their absolute flow, so a single "Blood flows FC"
scales their percentages while the uterus and the fetoplacental unit take a
growing share. If the fetoplacental flow is read as percent of cardiac output,
as its place under the "% of cardiac output" heading implies, the listed
percentages add to a near-constant total throughout pregnancy and after
delivery: the shared FC was calibrated to keep the budget. Read as L/h (the
unit of the Gaohua 2012 equation it is modelled on) the total would fall from
78% to about 68% at term.

```{r val-flow-budget}
budget <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    total = fq_adipose + fq_bone + fq_gonads + fq_heart + fq_skin + fq_thymus +
      fq_liver + fq_kidney + fq_muscle + fq_fetoplacental,
    total_if_lh = total - fq_fetoplacental + 100 * fq_fetoplacental / co
  )
budget |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 10, 20, 30, 39, 41, 50, 60)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, total, total_if_lh, fq_uterus, fq_fetoplacental) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-time, \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `GA (wk)` = time,
    `Sum of listed flows, % CO` = total,
    `Same, fetoplacental read as L/h` = total_if_lh,
    `Uterus, % CO` = fq_uterus,
    `Fetoplacental, % CO` = fq_fetoplacental
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Percent of cardiac output taken by the organs listed in Supplementary Table 2 (typical woman).")

stopifnot(
  # Percent reading: the budget stays within 3 percentage points of baseline.
  max(abs(budget$total - budget$total[budget$time == 0])) < 3,
  # L/h reading: the budget would lose more than 8 points near term.
  min(budget$total_if_lh) < budget$total[budget$time == 0] - 8
)
```

# Validation 4: the virtual population against Figure 1 and Supplementary Figure 1

```{r val-population}
pop_summ <- function(var) {
  sim_pop |>
    dplyr::group_by(time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      p05 = quantile(.data[[var]], 0.05),
      p50 = median(.data[[var]]),
      p95 = quantile(.data[[var]], 0.95),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
bw <- pop_summ("wt")
alb <- pop_summ("hsa")
co_p <- pop_summ("co")
qk <- pop_summ("q_kidney")

# Centres of the grey simulated clouds, read by eye. Figure 1A: body weight
# about 65 kg before pregnancy and about 75 kg at 36 to 40 weeks; Figure 1B:
# albumin falls from about 45 to about 34 g/L at term and is back
# near 45 g/L from about 45 weeks; Supplementary Figure 1c: cardiac output about
# 330 L/h before pregnancy and about 420 L/h through the second and third
# trimesters; Supplementary Figure 1d: renal blood flow about 60 L/h before and
# about 85 L/h at mid-pregnancy.
checks <- data.frame(
  Check = c("Body weight median, GA 0 (kg)", "Body weight median, GA 38 (kg)",
            "Albumin median, GA 0 (g/L)", "Albumin median, GA 38 (g/L)",
            "Albumin median, GA 50 (g/L)", "Cardiac output median, GA 0 (L/h)",
            "Cardiac output median, GA 30 (L/h)", "Renal blood flow median, GA 0 (L/h)",
            "Renal blood flow median, GA 20 (L/h)"),
  Model = c(bw$p50[bw$time == 0], bw$p50[bw$time == 38],
            alb$p50[alb$time == 0], alb$p50[alb$time == 38], alb$p50[alb$time == 50],
            co_p$p50[co_p$time == 0], co_p$p50[co_p$time == 30],
            qk$p50[qk$time == 0], qk$p50[qk$time == 20]),
  Figure = c(65, 75, 45, 34, 45, 330, 420, 60, 85)
)
checks$Model <- round(checks$Model, 1)
checks |>
  dplyr::rename(`Model (200 women)` = Model, `Read from figure` = Figure) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cohort medians against values read from the published figures.")

# Medians are robust to which women land in the tails; 15% covers reading the
# centre of a scatter cloud by eye.
stopifnot(all(abs(checks$Model / checks$Figure - 1) < 0.15))
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1A and 1B of Berton 2024: body weight and albumin against gestational age (200 virtual women; median and 5th to 95th percentiles)."}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(bw, var = "Body weight (kg)"),
  dplyr::mutate(alb, var = "Albumin (g/L)")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 40, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~var, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 66, by = 6)) +
  labs(x = "Gestational age (weeks)", y = NULL)
```

```{r fig-enzymes, fig.cap = "Replicates the fold-change shapes behind Figure 1C-1D and Supplementary Figure 2 of Berton 2024: liver enzyme abundance relative to the non-pregnant woman (typical values)."}
sim_typ |>
  dplyr::select(time, dplyr::all_of(unname(fc_cols[names(fc_cols) != "Albumin"]))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "enzyme", values_to = "fc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(enzyme = toupper(sub("fc_", "", enzyme))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, fc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 40, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~enzyme, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Gestational age (weeks)", y = "Fold change vs non-pregnant")
```

```{r fig-supp1, fig.cap = "Replicates Supplementary Figure 1c-1e of Berton 2024: cardiac output, renal blood flow and GFR (200 virtual women; median and 5th to 95th percentiles)."}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(co_p, var = "Cardiac output (L/h)"),
  dplyr::mutate(qk, var = "Renal blood flow (L/h)"),
  dplyr::mutate(pop_summ("gfr"), var = "GFR (mL/min)")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 40, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~var, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Gestational age (weeks)", y = NULL)
```

Figures 2 to 4 and Tables 2 and 3 of the paper are drug-exposure results of the
antiretroviral PBPK models, which are not part of this model.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Blood weight in pregnancy.** The Supplementary Table 2 row prints
  `Plasma weight * Plasma weight FC / (1 - 0.91*HCT) + RBC weight * RBC weight FC`.
  The first term is already a whole-blood weight, so the red cells are counted
  twice and blood weight more than doubles at term (+105% at 38 weeks). The
  Results state that blood weight is 47% higher in the third trimester. The
  model uses the sum of the two components, plasma x its FC plus red cells x
  their FC, which gives +48% at 38 weeks. Dividing the pregnant plasma weight by
  `1 - 0.91 * pregnant HCT` instead gives practically the same curve.
* **Fetoplacental flow units.** The row gives no unit. It is listed under the
  "Regional blood flows are expressed as % of cardiac output" heading and is
  read as percent of cardiac output; Validation 3 shows that this reading keeps
  the flow budget constant, which the L/h reading of the Gaohua 2012 equation
  it is modelled on does not. The coefficients differ from Gaohua 2012
  (refitted). The flow is zero before 2.23 weeks, where the cubic is negative,
  and after delivery. The row's printed range is "> 2.23 and < 40"; the model
  closes it at 40 weeks like every other pregnancy row, so that the flow and
  the fetoplacental weight end together at delivery.
* **Non-pregnant body surface area.** BSA appears both in the non-pregnant
  regressions (heart, muscle, spleen, liver, blood weights, cardiac output,
  brain and kidney flows, GFR) and as a pregnancy-wide row. The model evaluates
  the non-pregnant regressions with the non-pregnant BSA, so that gestational
  weight gain acts only through the printed fold changes, and reports `bsa` at
  the current body weight separately.
* **Distribution of the population CVs.** The paper gives a CV per quantity but
  not the distribution. The model uses the `normrnd(Mean, (CV/100) * Mean)` draw
  of the framework's published population generator (Stader 2019), so
  `Mean x (1 + eta)` with `eta ~ N(0, (CV/100)^2)`. For the widest CVs (mammary
  gland 51.65%, spleen 51.7%, thymus 44.8%) about 2% of draws are negative; the
  framework's handling of such draws in the 2020a generator is not published,
  and no truncation is applied here. The etas are independent.
* **Height and weight are generated, not covariates.** As in the paper's
  virtual population, height and non-pregnant body weight are drawn from their
  age regressions (CV 3.8% and 15.2%). Age is the only covariate; sex is fixed
  to female (`Sex = 1` in the framework convention).
* **Discontinuities at the knots are as printed.** Several fold changes jump at
  delivery (body weight, adipose, heart, plasma and uterus weights, uterine
  flow, the shared blood-flow FC) or at the week where they are capped at 1
  (red cells at 46.5 weeks, brain flow at 82.4 weeks). These reflect the
  printed equations. Two printed curves do not return to 1 inside 0 to 66 weeks
  (postpartum body weight and adipose weight), and the brain-flow FC is still
  1.23 at 60 weeks; they are used as printed.
* **Age range of the virtual cohort.** The paper draws age from a uniform
  distribution without stating the range for the development population; this
  vignette uses 18 to 44 years, the range of the verification trials
  (Supplementary Table 3).
* **Absolute enzyme abundances are not part of the model.** The paper reports
  only fold changes; the non-pregnant abundances in Figure 1C-1D come from the
  framework and are not printed. The fold changes apply equally to the liver
  and to the intestinal enzymes.
* **Organs without a printed row.** Lymph node and remaining-tissue weights and
  flows, lymph flow, and the hepatic-artery / portal split are part of the
  framework but have no Supplementary Table 2 row and are not modelled.
* **No PKNCA validation.** There is no drug and no concentration-time profile,
  so NCA does not apply. Validation uses the published third-trimester changes,
  Table 1, the blood-flow budget and the published figures instead.
